site.faq.account.a: For now, only on this device (in your browser's storage). Nothing is sent to a server. Clearing your browser data deletes it. Online sync is planned.
site.faq.free.a: Yes. MIDNIGHT JAPAN is a non-commercial fan project. There are no ads and nothing to buy.
site.faq.install.a: On Android (Chrome), tap “Install app” or use the menu → “Add to Home screen”. On iPhone/iPad (Safari), tap Share → “Add to Home Screen”. After the first load it also works offline.
site.faq.install.q: How do I install it on my phone?
site.faq.multi.a: Yes, in beta. Online meets are peer-to-peer: other players' cars appear in the same PA room, with no server cost. Expect the odd rough edge — it's still early.
site.faq.multi.q: Can I play online with friends?
site.faq.perf.a: Pick a lower graphics preset in Settings, close other tabs, and make sure hardware acceleration is enabled in your browser.
site.faq.perf.q: The game runs slowly. What can I do?
site.faq.real.a: It's a faithful but approximate recreation for fun. If you visit the real PA, please be quiet, don't block the lots, and follow the instructions of the police and PA staff — it is often closed at night on weekends.
site.faq.real.q: Is this the real Daikoku PA?
site.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
site.feat.cars.d: From R32 to R35, AE86 to GR86, FD3S, NSX and kei cars to EVs and patrol cars — each with catalogue specs.
site.feat.city.d: 421,000 real buildings, 53,000 streets, rail lines and rivers of Yokohama and Kawasaki from OpenStreetMap — houses with tiled roofs, mansions with balconies, shop streets, factories — all drivable.
site.feat.city.t: A real city, not a backdrop
site.feat.cycle.d: 30 minutes of play = 12 hours on the clock. Watch the Bay Bridge light up and the factory skyline glow after sunset.
site.feat.ev.d: Three regenerative-braking levels plus one-pedal driving, with the near-silent whine of an electric motor.
site.feat.langs.d: Play in Korean, Japanese, English and 17 more languages — switch anytime from the menu.
site.feat.manual.d: Turn the key, feather the clutch, row an H-pattern box — and yes, you can stall it. Automatics get P/R/N/D and a handbrake.
site.feat.online.d: Free peer-to-peer online: other players' cars show up in the same PA room. No game servers, so it stays free.
site.feat.pa.d: The car park, the 24-hour store, the food court, the vending-machine row and the spiral JCT loops around it — modelled on the real place.
site.feat.plates.d: White private, green commercial, yellow kei and black kei-commercial plates — each car wears the right one.
site.feat.police.d: Patrol cars cruise the PA. Get too loud and you'll hear the loudspeaker — or watch the PA get closed for the night.
site.feat.radio.d: Four stations of original city pop, eurobeat, lo-fi and enka-style tunes. Open a door and everyone hears it.
site.feat.toll.d: ETC and cash lanes, barrier arms and separate fares for standard cars and kei cars at the Daikoku-futō exit.
site.feat.tune.d: Stock, Street, Grip, Drift, Wangan and Touge presets, or tune power, weight, tyres, gearing, brakes, balance, downforce and steering lock yourself.
site.feat.walk.d: Step out, pick your outfit, grab a drink from the vending machines and check out other people's builds.
site.features.lead: Everything that makes a night at Daikoku special — the loops, the lights, the cars and the people.
site.features.title: The car meet, recreated
site.footer.about: A free browser car-meet game set at Daikoku PA on the Shuto Expressway, Yokohama. Made by fans, for the night.
site.footer.disclaimer: Non-commercial fan project. Vehicle names and trademarks belong to their owners. Not affiliated with Shuto Expressway, NEXCO, or Kanagawa Prefectural Police.
